ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in a triangular piece of paper $ABC$, $\angle B = 90^\circ$, $AB = 3$. Point $D$ is on side $BC$. When $\triangle ABD$ is folded along the straight line $AD$, point $B$ exactly falls on point $E$ on the side $AC$. If $AD = CD$, what is the length of $AC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} It follows from the property of folding that $AE=AB=3$,\\
$\angle AED=90^\circ$ \\
$\because AD=CD$ \\
$\therefore \triangle ADC$ is an isosceles triangle \\
$\because DE\perp AC$ \\
$\therefore EC=AE$ \\
$\therefore AC=\boxed{6}$

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: A is above-left, B is below A with a right-angle mark at B, C is to the right on the same baseline as B, D lies on BC, E lies on AC, and segments AD and DE are drawn. From the text, AB=3, folding triangle ABD along AD sends B to E, and AD=CD. Use the folding property: A and D stay fixed, so AE=AB=3, and the right angle at B maps to a right angle at E, giving DE perpendicular to AC. Since AD=CD, triangle ADC is isosceles with base AC.
